title: About
text:
My background is in statistical physics: finding structure in systems that are large, noisy, and only partially observable. During my PhD I worked on community detection in complex networks, extreme value statistics, and synchronization in nonlinear dynamical systems — problems where the honest answer is a distribution, not a point estimate, and where getting the uncertainty right matters as much as getting the estimate right.
That same discipline is what draws me to quantitative finance. Credit risk, derivatives pricing, and factor research all come down to the same core problem: build a model that is precise enough to be useful, honest about what it doesn’t know, and robust when the data stops behaving the way your assumptions assumed it would.

title: About

How I work
I like problems that sit at the boundary between rigorous theory and messy real-world data — extreme value theory applied to tail risk, uncertainty quantification applied to model validation, network methods applied to systemic risk. I write my own tooling rather than treating models as black boxes, because being able to explain why a model says what it says is usually the difference between a model that survives model risk review and one that doesn’t.
I’m currently looking for roles in quantitative research, model validation, and model risk — credit risk, market risk, or systematic equity research.

title: Projects

Credit Risk

Credit Risk & Capital Modeling
End-to-end PD/LGD/EAD framework on Lending Club consumer loans, assessed against Basel III IRB, IFRS 9, and SR 11-7 expectations. Benchmarks WOE/IV scorecards against LightGBM and a Merton structural model, then runs Gaussian copula Monte Carlo for expected loss and regulatory capital across the full portfolio.

title: Tania Ghosh
text:
I build and validate quantitative models for credit risk and systematic equity research. My work covers PD/LGD/EAD frameworks and Basel III capital, derivatives pricing under stochastic volatility, and NLP-driven signals built from unstructured financial text.
I hold a PhD in Computational Statistical Physics from the University of Houston, where I developed algorithms for finding structure in large, noisy, high-dimensional systems and built uncertainty quantification methods using extreme value theory. The same problems recur in finance: estimating things from data that is messy, non-stationary, and short on ground truth.
I am currently looking for quantitative research, model validation, and model risk roles.
